_comment: The airfield (SPEC.md §13, M29): mission 2's map, in the same shape as data/map.json. rows are row-major: rows[r] is board row r, and character i in that row is the hex at axial q = rowQStart(r) + i. Terrain ids must exist in data/terrain.json; the desert's are printed in the one ground colour, desert ochre (SPEC.md §11).
name: The landing ground at Bir el Kasra
_dropRuns: SPEC.md §9, §13. All three land outside the wire. West drops straight down outside the west wire, over the dunes and the escarpment (M29c, the operator's: M29's West ran diagonally across the wire, where a man could land on it and the car), north along the scrub above the north wire, where the outer patrol walks, and south along the sand below the south wire, closest to the Ju 52s and the bowser (M29b, the operator's: it replaced an East run from the north-east corner, too like the North, and uses the bottom rows). `tag`, `labelAlong`, `labelNudge`, `windAlong` as in data/map.json.

dropRuns.label: West run
dropRuns.description: Straight down outside the west wire: soft dunes and the escarpment, nothing to land on but sand and rock, and the car kept out by the wire. The longest walk to the aircraft.

dropRuns.label: North run
dropRuns.description: The scrub along the north wire: firm landings and the gate close by. A patrol walks the wire: pack your chutes.

dropRuns.label: South run
dropRuns.description: The sand south of the wire: down closest to the Ju 52s and the bowser, under the south AA pit's eye, and in the open.

_enemies: SPEC.md §6, §13. The two AA pits and the signals tent's guard are posts; a guard walks each dispersal, the outer patrol walks the scrub above the north wire (where the north run lands), a patrol walks the sand below the south wire (M30b: where the south run lands; with the default timer at 4 turns the South won 91% on Normal, 53% on Hard), a patrol walks the sand under the escarpment outside the west wire (M30: where the west run lands, whose chutes nobody found, and which won nineteen games in twenty), a patrol walks the camp, a guard stands among the south-east tents (M29b, the operator's), and the perimeter car drives the track round inside the wire. The car is its own type, `vehicle` (the manifest's counter-enemy-vehicle) (data/missions.json enemies patch): fast, and it cannot be killed.
_reserve: SPEC.md §6. The airfield's defence company turns out from the camp at Alarmed and marches round to guard the last stretch before the trucks.
_reinforcements: SPEC.md §6. By lorry down the road from the east edge, to posts on the ways into the rendezvous. None are called on Normal (rules.json objectives.<kind>.reinforcements).
_objectives: SPEC.md §7, §13. Eight aircraft, each in its pen: the pen hex behind it is its one charge point. The fuel bowser stands on the south apron between the middle two Ju 52s; its charge point is the one hex beside it whose blast takes in those two and no others (for M30's rule that it sets them off). The signals tent is the airfield's telephone exchange: blown, or its line cut by a scout. None is primary: the win is any N aircraft (data/missions.json). `art` (optional, art only) picks which picture of its kind is drawn: the Stukas' or the Ju 52s'. `stampNudge` (M31d, optional, art only) moves its DESTROYED stamp by [x, y] hex radii, only while an objective beside it is destroyed too: the bowser's goes up and the Ju 52's beside it down, so the two stamps do not print over each other (the operator's).
_exfil: SPEC.md §10, §13. The rendezvous with the trucks, at the wadi's mouth in the south-west corner. `exfilArt` (art only) picks its picture: the trucks, where France has the barn. `exfilNoteNudge` (M29c, art only) moves the exfil ring's note by [x, y] hex radii: inside the ring here, the operator's. `exfilArtNudge` (M31d, art only) moves the exfil's picture the same way: the trucks lifted, as the bottom one was cut off by the board's edge (the operator's). `dropCueAt` (M29b, art only) is the hex PICK A DROP DIRECTION centres on: the strip.
_diversionRun: M31, art only: the jeep raid (the mission's diversion) drives one of these lines, from off the board to off it, outside the wire, its guns (on its left) toward the field: along the north scrub east to west, along the south sand west to east, or down the west edge. When it is called it takes the line with the fewest counters near it (M31, the operator's: it drove through chips), first in this order on a tie.
_places: SPEC.md §11. Art only. Placeholder names for the operator to reword. Kind `wadi` (M31d) prints the name solid over the wadi's stones, one hex up the wadi from its mouth (the operator's).
